column11: DELIVERED by ACBP-FE-003 (squash 0243d52) and CORRECTED by squash 86117c0 after an independent adversarial review returned 13 findings. THE EVIDENCE LINE ASKS FOR A MECHANISM THIS APP DELIBERATELY DOES NOT HAVE: there are no "authenticated and unauthenticated redirects" because clerkMiddleware "protects NOTHING automatically" (proxy.ts, its own words), enforcement is explicit per handler, and console screens that read real data render an honest refusal instead of bouncing. apps/web/src/app/(site)/auth-surfaces.test.ts pins that decision against NINE redirect idioms - including the three that name no path at all (redirectToSignIn, RedirectToSignIn, auth.protect()) and router.push, already this repo's own navigation idiom - and scans next.config.ts, which can declare async redirects() and sat outside the original scan root. Four mutations applied, four killed, each AssertionError read from the run. THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS GUARD WAS LARGELY VACUOUS AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED: it caught one spelling nobody would write; its refusal sweep matched a FILENAME so it checked four of six surfaces while its name said "every" (portfolio-view.ts and company-view.ts hold their refusal copy in .ts view builders); and its toContain('unauthenticated') ran on RAW TEXT including header comments, so deleting the real COPY arm from provisioning-refusal.tsx left it green - the mutation that supposedly proved it had been run against a different file. NOT MET AND DISCLOSED rather than implied: the label/aria-describedby binding and the bounded envelope on a failed credential exchange are Clerk's DOM and Clerk's exchange, unreachable from this app (SignInProps exposes appearance only; @clerk/elements is not a dependency). A THIRD "disclosure" WAS REMOVED AS FALSE - appearance.elements exposes socialButtonsRoot, so code here CAN reach those buttons; that line is in any case this row's Explicit exclusions cell, not a criterion. A FALSE CLAIM SHIPPED IN 0243d52 AND IS CORRECTED IN 86117c0: "every console screen renders an honest unauthenticated refusal" is not true of /console itself, which has no authorization check on the page or its layout; it is entirely mock and says so on screen so nothing real leaks, and a test now pins that premise so the day it reads real data the guard fails. FRAME DEFECTS FIXED: globals.css clamps main to 40rem so the auth ground painted a 640px stripe under a full-width header; the six design tokens site.css used were declared ONLY in console.css, which these routes never import, so every var() fell through to a literal and a light theme would have flipped /console alone (tokens moved to globals.css, fallbacks removed so an absent token breaks visibly); and 100vh under a sibling header guaranteed a scrollbar on every visit. Exact-head CI green at zero skips: 32130057599 on 582c77a, and 32133786383 on 89f06cf at 298 files / 4453 tests.
